name: 2129 S. Indiana Avenue — Bane Brothers' livery stable at 2129-2131 (district draft; refined by T-1946)

function.note: The 1911 sheet reads '3-storey brick building lettered GARAGE, auto repairing on the second floor, wood-working and painting on the third, an office on the first, two rows of iron columns each floor'. In 1904 this was Bane Brothers' livery and boarding stables, which the Blue Book for that year advertises at 2125, 2127 and 2129 Indiana Avenue; the same address was a horse livery until 1910 and the West Motor Livery Co.'s garage by 1911, so the sheet's garage is read as the livery's stable kept in use (T-3013). Carried to 1904 on the T-3009 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

research_note: A DISTRICT DRAFT (T-3009, the owner's district pass of 2026-10-08): a serviceable first model, complete from the street, the walks, the alley and the air, that T-1946 refines in place under this same id. Written by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py from the sheet 35w trace (s35wfp-indiana_2129-b1), the T-3009 census (s35w-2129-front) and the T-1837 register row frontage-35w-2129–2131; every height, roof, opening and feature is the draft rules' reconstruction (data/components/prairie_1904/draft_prairie_1904.json; liberty L-draft-district-background-3009).

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-3009 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.
